changes: Notes now say that the catalogue date (~1569 AD) does not match the stated conversion rule (LS 429 + 1119 = 1548). ce_approx stays 1548.
Residence changed to '...pura (village)'. The colophon says '...puragrāmīyai[ḥ]', meaning 'residents of the village ...pura'; the beginning of the name is lost.
Notes now say that 'puragrāmīya' gives where the scribes lived, which is not necessarily where the copy was made.
Notes now say that 'Brāhmaṇa' might be a caste word rather than a name. It is kept as a name because it has its own 'śrī'.

notes: The three co-scribes are named together in one compound: śrīśrīrāmaśrībrāhmaṇaśrībhīmair likhitaṃ. Each name has its own śrī. That supports reading 'Brāhmaṇa' as a personal name, as the cataloguer does, but it could be a caste word. The text before 'puragrāmīyai[ḥ]' is lost (lacuna), so the village name is incomplete. The word describes where the scribes lived and may not be the place of copying. Date: LS 429 + 1119 gives about 1548 CE. The catalogue's '~1569 AD' does not match that rule; it is probably a miscalculation in the catalogue.
